documents.text: Homeowner Expanded Analyses Package _____________________________________________________ Collection Procedures: Sample from a sink in the house or a spigot close to the well head, never from a hose. If the tap has an aerator, it should be removed. Sterilize the sampling point with flame or bleach, and then flush for 2 minutes. Fill up the provided bottles, being certain to fill the clear plastic bottle with the banded cap to slightly over the 100mL fill line. Keep the samples on ice during transport to the laboratory. Arsenic (As) by EPA 200.8 C D P H r e g u l a t e s a maximum of 10.0 ug/L for public water systems Boron (B) by EPA 200.8 EPA has no drinking water guidelines. Many sensitive crops are affected by 500 ug/L – 2,000 ug/L, and only tolerant crops produce yields in the 2,000 ug/L – 10,000 ug/L range. Your final report includes an evaluation of all results submitted by your laboratory to ERA. The assigned value(s) and acceptance limits were not available to your laboratory at or before the time of reporting. All analytes in ERA's QuiK ™ Response program are evaluated using the following tiered approach. If the analyte is listed in the most current TNI Fields of Proficiency Testing (FoPT) tables the evaluation was completed by comparing the reported result to the acceptance limits generated using the criteria contained in the tables and the evaluation criteria contained in the 2016 TNI Standard, Volume 3 . If the analyte is not included in the TNI FoPT tables, the reported result has been evaluated using the procedures outlined in ERA's Standard Operating Procedure for the Generation of Performance Acceptance Limits (SOP 730002268 ). All analytes are included in ERA's A 2 LA accreditation, certification number 1539.01 . documents.text: 6390 Joyce Drive # 100 Golden, CO 80403 Phone 303-940-0033 Fax 866-283-0269 www.phenova.com August 7, 2025 Ms. Thia Bachman Alpha Analytical Laboratories - Ukiah 208 Mason Street Ukiah, CA 95482 USA Dear Thia, Thank you for participating in the WPM0725 Water Pollution Proficiency Testing Study. Enclosed is your final report, which has been carefully reviewed by the PT specialists at Phenova. This report presents some additional sections and features which will give you more information on the study data for the standards that were reported by your laboratory and more information regarding the overall performance of your laboratory in relation to other study participants. The enclosed report is in two sections, the "Evaluation Report" and the "Statistical Report". The "Evaluation Report" contains the evaluation of your reported data as well the reported method, analysis date and analyst. The "Evaluation Report" is an updated and enhanced version of the reports you previously received at the conclusion of our PT studies. The "Statistical Report" contains your passing percentage as well as statistics from the study for the analytes reported by your laboratory. For any analyte falling outside the established acceptance limits, our PT management staff would like to assist you in determining the most appropriate course of corrective action for your facility. Please contact us at any time if we may be of service to you. Thank you again for participating in the WPM0725 Water Pollution Proficiency Testing Study. We appreciate working with you and look forward to our next study. If you have any questions, please call us at 866-942-2978. documents.text: frm_CA_PT_R1.00 Form approved: TB 01-2023 Page 1 of 2 C orrective Action Date: 09/24/2025 Department: BAL Wet Chem Initiated by: Proficiency Testing (PT) Failure CA#: BA-CA-25-6 Study ID: R41807 Sample ID: 25I1113 – WP Residual Chlorine Batch ID: AI54482 Analysis Date: 09/06/2025 Analyte: Total Residual Chlorine, Residual Free Chlorine Method: SM 4500-Cl G-2011 ELAP FOA Code: 108.114 Reference/Requirement: TNI 2016 V1M1 6.1 & 6.2 A laboratory that fails to successfully analyze a PT study for a particular FOA shall determine the root cause of the failure and take [and document] corrective action [and root cause]. Description of non-conforming work: PT result for Total and Free Chlorine failed low. Total Chlorine - Reported: 1.1 mg/L ; Assigned Value = 2.31 mg/L Free Chlorine – Reported: 1.1 mg/L ; Assigned Value = 2.31 mg/L Root Cause: Phenova PT and QC samples were analyzed in both LR and HR mode for confirmation. QC Readings confirmed to be within acceptable range per the certificate of analysis. Samples were labeled with lot numbers indicated on volumetric flask. Work orders were not provided as the PTs were not logged beforehand. These lot numbers were also recorded on the bench sheet. The QC data was inputted into the PT (Work Order) data rows, and Technical Manager was not able to review/confirm data prior to Phenova data submittal. Corrective Action Plan: 1. The Quality Director (QD) will re-order the PT with QC 2. One sample control person must log in Phenova PT & QC on site prior to analysis. Packing list should be carefully matched to PT containers (ampoules, bottles, etc.). For any discrepancies, notify Quality Manager or directly contact Phenova. 3. Laboratory must re-review analysis SOP. 4. Laboratory staff should prepare and analyze QC by both total and free chlorine before starting PT. Results should be compared against certificate of analysis to check that they’re within the acceptable range. If passing, laboratory should then proceed to preparing and analyzing PT sample following same procedure. If an error in preparation is suspected , PT/QC sample should be prepared again from concentrate provided in ampoule. If insufficient concentrate is available, notify QM to re-order PT/QC. 5. Physical bench sheets must be uploaded to LIMS batch for Technical Manager to review. 6. Technical Manager must review LIMS data prior to Phenova data upload and submittal. Description of non-conforming work: PT Result for Color failed low. Reported 30 CU, assigned value = 45 CU Root Cause: Color Standards were prepared on 03/24/2025. The PT sample was prepared and analyzed per Phenova instructions on 04/01/2025. The prepared PT sample was poured off , further diluted according to the SOP, and compared to each color standard. Corrective Action Plan: 1. The Quality Manager (QM) will instruct TM and analysts to prepare a new set of Color Standards following the SOP. 2. The TM will review PT instruction sheet with analysts and will train on carefully following instructions.
